title: Being good company
hook: be the sangat someone else needs
tomorrow: Bebe slipped in the chili garden. Ardas first, or the ER?

segments.voice: Yesterday, small sangats: the kind village scattered, carrying the good. Small and true, three people and a gutka in a parking lot. Then one of the three stopped coming.

A hoodie borrowed from a friend comes back smelling like their house: their soap, their kitchen, their dog. Nobody did that on purpose. Two Tuesdays later, Navi's spot in the parking lot is empty, and Simran has a long text half-written: why sangat matters, three paragraphs, two Gurbani lines. Bebe reads it over her shoulder and says, too much perfume. Then she points Simran to a shalok of Kabir about a tree that never says a word.
screen: `A HOODIE SMELLS LIKE THEIR HOUSE.` → `THREE PARAGRAPHS TO NAVI.` → `A TREE THAT NEVER SAYS A WORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the puzzle. On Ang 1365, Kabir says, in paraphrase: the sandalwood tree is good, even surrounded by scrubby trees; the ones that live near it become fragrant like sandalwood. The sandalwood does nothing. It doesn't move, doesn't argue, doesn't send three paragraphs. So how does it change its neighbors? By being what it is, close by, for a long time. Fragrance works by nearness, not by force. And in the very next shalok Kabir adds the twist: the bamboo, swollen with its own tallness, can live right beside the sandalwood and never pick up the scent. Being good company isn't a technique you aim at someone. It's a way of being near, steady and warm, that a person can breathe in if they're open, and that you can't force on anyone who isn't. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: in Kabir's picture, good company is a smell, not a speech. Simran deletes the three paragraphs. She sends one line instead: saved you a spot, no pressure, we're getting fries after. Navi doesn't answer that night. Two days later a thumbs up arrives. She keeps the spot saved.
screen: `ANG 1365: THE SANDALWOOD TREE.` · `FRAGRANCE BY NEARNESS, NOT FORCE.` · `THE BAMBOO NEVER PICKS IT UP.` · `ONE LINE: SAVED YOU A SPOT.` · then, large: `BE GOOD COMPANY.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person who might need company right now: someone who's gone quiet, or stopped showing up. Don't plan a speech. Just picture sitting near them, steady and unhurried, for the whole sit, as the sandalwood sits near its neighbors.
Being good company. Being the steady, warm presence someone else can breathe in, near and unforced, like the sandalwood tree.
Keep this one: be good company, a smell, not a speech. Day 1717, a spot saved.

screen: `DAY 1717 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 91 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: BEBE SLIPPED. ARDAS FIRST, OR THE ER?`

howItsDone: In Sikh life, being good company can look like checking in on someone who has stopped coming to the gurdwara, bringing them to langar, or simply sitting with them, without lecturing.

match.prompt: Kabir's two trees — tap the pairs.
pairs: become like sandalwood by living near
tall, proud, never picks up the scent
saved you a spot, no pressure

myth: being good company means persuading someone with the right argument
the sandalwood never argues; its fragrance works by nearness, not force.
in Kabir's shaloks, the bamboo lives beside the sandalwood and stays unscented
proud of its height, it never picks up the fragrance.
if you're good company, everyone near you will change
the bamboo shows the limit: you can't force it on anyone who isn't open.

fork.setup: a friend has skipped your study group for a month. you are tempted to send a long message about commitment. what does Kabir's tree suggest?
options: a short, warm line that leaves the door open, then keep showing up.
a clear explanation of why the group matters, so they understand.
say nothing at all; good company never reaches out first.
fork.reveal: the sandalwood changes its neighbors by being near and steady. a saved spot, not a speech; and some, like the bamboo, won't take it in.

original.note: Gurmukhi: chandan, sandalwood, Kabir's picture of the good company whose fragrance spreads.

trapdoor: what you thought: good company means giving good advice.
what it means: good company is a steady, warm presence others can breathe in by being near, and it can't be forced.
what a scholar hears: Kabir's shaloks on Ang 1365: the sandalwood among scrub trees (shalok 11) and the proud bamboo that stays unscented (shalok 12).
guess: being a steady, warm presence others can breathe in
always having the right advice when friends struggle
inviting as many people as possible to a gurdwara

chat.says: navi finally sent a thumbs up. do i send the 3 paragraphs now that he's listening??
options: nah. keep the spot saved and keep showing up. a smell, not a speech.
yes, now's the moment, he's finally open to the full argument.
no, stop texting entirely; he has to come back on his own.
chat.meaning: Kabir's sandalwood changes its neighbors by nearness, not force. Steady warmth works; a lecture is the bamboo's tall pride.

Kabir.meaning: a bhagat whose hymns appear in the Guru Granth Sahib

shalok.meaning: a short verse in the Guru Granth Sahib

sandalwood.meaning: a fragrant tree; in Kabir, the picture of good company

Ang.meaning: a page of the Guru Granth Sahib; literally a limb

sources.ref: Ang 1365, Salok Kabir 11 (chandan kaa birvaa bhalaa), paraphrased
Ang 1365, Salok Kabir 12 (baans badaaee boodiaa), paraphrased
